bugs.explanation: Adding `role="button"` to a `<div>` creates a custom button that still lacks native keyboard interaction (Enter/Space activation, focus management). Use a real `<button>` element which provides all this natively.

bugs.fix:
<button type="button" onclick="close()" aria-label="Close dialog">
  <svg aria-hidden="true"><!-- x icon --></svg>
</button>
bugs.explanation: Buttons with only icon content have no accessible name. Add `aria-label` to the button to provide a text description for screen readers, and add `aria-hidden="true"` to the SVG so it's not read separately.

`aria-expanded` communicates the open/closed state of a controlled element to screen readers. Without it, users know a button exists but can't tell if the menu is currently visible. Toggle the value between `true`/`false` when the menu opens/closes.

`aria-current="page"` identifies the current page in a navigation list. Screen readers announce it, and you can style it with `[aria-current='page']`. Without it, keyboard and screen reader users can't easily tell which page they're on.

When content changes dynamically (status messages, notifications, form errors), `aria-live` instructs screen readers to announce the change. `aria-live="polite"` announces after current speech finishes. Use `assertive` only for urgent messages.

`role="alert"` (equivalent to `aria-live="assertive"`) interrupts the current speech to announce the content immediately. Use it for error messages. Use `role="status"` (polite) for non-critical updates like form success messages.

bugs.fix:
Skip to main content
...
...
bugs.explanation: A 'Skip to main content' link allows keyboard users to bypass repetitive navigation. It's typically visually hidden until focused (`:focus-visible { position: static; }`). It's an WCAG 2.4.1 (Level A) requirement.

Title

Content
bugs.explanation: When opening a modal, focus must move into it, and when closing, return to the trigger. The native `<dialog>` element with `.showModal()` handles focus trapping automatically. Also add `aria-labelledby` referencing the modal title.

title: tabindex 0 vs Positive
code:
First tab stop
Second tab stop

bugs.fix:
First tab stop
Second tab stop
bugs.explanation: Positive `tabindex` values create a custom tab order that can be confusing and conflict with the natural DOM order. Use `tabindex="0"` to make non-interactive elements focusable in DOM order, and rely on source order for tab sequence.

`tabindex="-1"` makes an element focusable by JavaScript (`.focus()`) but not through Tab key navigation. This is useful for error messages that you want to scroll to and focus programmatically after form submission.

title: aria-describedby for Help Text
code: Must be at least 8 characters

bugs.fix: Must be at least 8 characters
bugs.explanation: `aria-describedby` links the input to its supplementary description. Screen readers announce the label first, then the description when the field is focused. Without it, the help text is visually adjacent but programmatically disconnected.

title: role img for SVG
code:
<svg width="100" height="100">
  <circle cx="50" cy="50" r="40" fill="red"/>
</svg>

bugs.fix:
<svg role="img" aria-label="Red circle" width="100" height="100">
  <title>Red circle</title>
  <circle cx="50" cy="50" r="40" fill="red"/>
</svg>
bugs.explanation: Inline SVGs aren't automatically announced by screen readers. Add `role="img"` and `aria-label` (or a `<title>` element as the first child) so screen readers can describe the graphic. For decorative SVGs, add `aria-hidden="true"`.

Light gray `#999` on white has a contrast ratio of ~2.85:1, which fails WCAG AA (minimum 4.5:1 for normal text). Use a darker gray like `#595959` (~7.0:1) or `#767676` (~4.54:1) to meet the minimum requirement.

title: Don't Convey Info by Color Alone

bugs.explanation: WCAG 1.4.1 requires that information isn't conveyed by color alone. Users who are color blind may not perceive the red. Add a text indicator (e.g., ✗, 'Error:') or icon so the meaning is clear independent of color.

WCAG 2.5.5 (Level AAA) recommends touch targets be at least 44×44 CSS pixels. Even at Level AA (WCAG 2.5.8), targets must be at least 24×24. Small touch targets cause errors on mobile. Increase the clickable area with padding or min-width/min-height.

Placeholder text disappears as the user types, leaving them without context. It also has poor contrast by default and is not announced consistently by screen readers. Always use a `<label>` for the accessible name; use placeholder only for example values, not labels.

The `autocomplete` attribute with standardized values (like `given-name`, `email`, `current-password`) enables browser and password manager autofill. This is critical for accessibility (WCAG 1.3.5) and significantly improves form completion rates.

Error messages should be adjacent to their field and programmatically linked via `aria-describedby`. Also set `aria-invalid="true"` on the input when invalid. This ensures both sighted and screen reader users receive error feedback at the correct field.

title: Language Switch
code: The French word for hello is bonjour.

bugs.fix: The French word for hello is bonjour.
bugs.explanation: When a word or phrase is in a different language than the page's `lang`, wrap it in an element with the appropriate `lang` attribute. This allows screen readers to switch pronunciation rules for the foreign word.

title: Reading Level and Plain Language
code: The utilization of obfuscated nomenclature constitutes a significant impediment to comprehension accessibility.

bugs.fix: Using complex words makes content harder to understand.
bugs.explanation: WCAG 3.1.5 recommends content be readable at a lower secondary education level or supplemented with simpler alternatives. Plain language reduces cognitive load and improves accessibility for users with cognitive disabilities or non-native speakers.
